newsitem.title: ITALY: Ciampi - Italy does not plan competitive devaluation.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi - Italy does not plan competitive devaluation.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Monday that his country did not plan to follow a policy of devaluation by pushing the lira's rate lower within Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism.
European Union officials agreed late on Sunday to re-admit the lira to the semi-fixed exchange rate system that it was forced out of in 1992 due to intense market speculation.

But the central parity rate chosen for the currency was higher than Italy had requested, throwing open the question of whether Italy would try to push the level of its currency lower in the open market.
The conditions of Italy's entry to the exchange rate mechanism allow the currency to fluctuate in a 15 percent band around the central parity rate of 990 lire to the mark.
"We do not intend to use this fluctuation band to improve the international competitiveness of our economy," Ciampi told a group of German journalists in Rome on Monday evening.
He added that, on the contrary, Italy's re-joining of the ERM had to be seen as a decisive step in its bid to join Economic and Monetary Union and its single currency from the start in 1999.
Stable currency rates are just one of a series of economic conditions that would-be EMU participants must meet in 1997, alongside targets on budgets, inflation and interest rates.

Ciampi said he was firmly opposed to the idea of postponing the intended launch date for the planned Euro, a suggestion sometimes tabled as a means to counter the extreme problems some nations face in meeting the entry criteria.
"I am opposed to any delay in the start of EMU," he said.
He added that the lira's EMS return also opened up scope for further interest rate cuts in Italy, particularly at the short end of the interest rate spectrum.
"Larger interest rate falls can be expected in the area of short-term interest rates than in the area of long-term rates," he said.
